red_quiz.prompt: Twenty-plus AIS tracks collapse onto Gelendzhik Airport inland. Speeds flip 0 kn / 100 kn. What CLASS?
choices: GNSS spoofing feeding AIS (coherent false airport fix)
red_quiz.teach: Many ships, one inland airport, cartoon speeds = spoofed PNT. Not parking.

pins.name: Crimea Approaches — Second Airport Stack
pins.anomaly_class: Mass AIS at an inland field

red_quiz.prompt: Same hour: ~50 tracks at Simferopol field, ~30 at Gelendzhik. What does the PAIR tell you?
choices: Two busy cargo airports on the water
Two spoof aim-points, one regional event — not two bad boxes
ADS-B mixed into AIS by accident
red_quiz.teach: Two land fields at once is a theater event.

red_quiz.prompt: Plot says west Black Sea off Romania. A receiver at Kerch hears the same VHF. What CLASS?
choices: Plot is a lie — VHF cannot be both Romania and heard at Kerch
red_quiz.teach: AIS VHF is short-range. Impossible RF path beats the pretty line.

red_quiz.prompt: Receivers drop lock. No shared fake airport. What CLASS?
choices: Jamming / denial — loss of fix, not a coherent false position
red_quiz.teach: Jam = silence. Spoof = many ships agree on a wrong place.

pins.name: Aviation Twin — Circle Track
pins.anomaly_class: Circle geometry on a PNT feed

red_quiz.prompt: A PNT feed draws a tight circle over land for many tracks. Closest CLASS?
choices: Spoofed geometry (crop-circle family) — not a real racetrack
red_quiz.teach: Same lie as Hormuz tankers in a circle.

red_quiz.prompt: You see a real MMSI on a public map. What do you do in this range?
choices: Hunt it and write the owner
Leave it. This hour uses fictional twins only
red_quiz.teach: Public cases teach the class. Live hunts are out.
